title: Minimal Polynomial vs Characteristic Polynomial of Matrices
description: Formalizes the fundamental relationship between minimal and characteristic polynomials of matrices: minpoly K M divides charpoly M, both are monic, minpoly annihilates M (Cayley-Hamilton variant), and roots of minpoly are roots of charpoly. 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The characteristic polynomial det(λI − M) was central to Cauchy's eigenvalue work (1829) and formalized by Weierstrass (1858) in the context of bilinear forms. The Cayley-Hamilton theorem — every matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial — was announced by Cayley for 2×2 and 3×3 cases in 1858 and by Hamilton for quaternions the same year; the full n×n proof was given by Frobenius (1878) using invariant factors and the rational canonical form. The minimal polynomial emerged from Frobenius's invariant factor theory: m_M is the largest invariant factor of (λI − M), equivalently the GCD of all (n−1)×(n−1) minors of (λI − M) divided by the GCD of all entries. The fundamental theorem minpoly | charpoly follows from Cayley-Hamilton (charpoly annihilates M) and the universal property of minpoly (it divides any annihilating polynomial). The minimal polynomial governs the primary decomposition of K^n as a K[X]-module and determines the Jordan structure: M is diagonalizable over K iff minpoly has no repeated roots; M has a cyclic vector iff minpoly = charpoly. This file provides the foundational infrastructure for Jordan normal form theory in Lean 4.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: (1) minpoly K M divides charpoly M. (2) Both are monic. (3) charpoly annihilates M (Cayley-Hamilton). (4) minpoly degree ≤ dim(M). (5) Roots of minpoly are roots of charpoly.
overview.proofStrategy: Most results follow from Mathlib's minpoly and charpoly APIs. minpoly_dvd_charpoly: use minpoly.dvd and charpoly_monic. charpoly_annihilates: Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly. minpoly_annihilates: minpoly.aeval.
keyInsights: **Divisibility**: minpoly(M) | charpoly(M) because charpoly(M)[M] = 0 (Cayley-Hamilton) and minpoly(M) divides any annihilating polynomial.
**Degree bounds**: deg(minpoly) ≤ n = dim(K^n) since the n+1 matrices {I, M, M², ..., M^n} are linearly dependent in Mat_n(K).
**Root relationship**: Every root of minpoly is a root of charpoly (divisibility). The converse may fail (Jordan blocks).
**Cayley-Hamilton**: charpoly(M)(M) = 0 — the matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial.

**Universal property generates the annihilator ideal**: minpoly generates Ann(M) = {p ∈ K[X] | p(M) = 0} as a principal ideal. Equivalently, p(M) = 0 iff minpoly | p. This makes minpoly the unique 'canonical' annihilating polynomial from which all others derive.

sections.title: Parts 1–2: Integrality and Divisibility
sections.summary: matrix_is_integral: every matrix is integral over its base ring (prerequisite for minpoly). minpoly_dvd_charpoly: minpoly K M | M.charpoly — the core divisibility theorem. minpoly_monic: minpoly is monic. minpoly_degree_pos: degree ≥ 1 for nontrivial matrix rings.

sections.title: Part 3: Degree Bounds
sections.summary: minpoly_degree_le_charpoly_degree: deg(minpoly) ≤ deg(charpoly) via Polynomial.natDegree_le_of_dvd. minpoly_degree_le_dim: deg(minpoly) ≤ n via Matrix.charpoly_natDegree_eq_dim. Both use charpoly_monic.ne_zero to ensure the divisor is nonzero.

sections.title: Parts 4–5: Annihilation, Universal Property, Monicness
sections.summary: charpoly_annihilates: aeval M M.charpoly = 0 (Cayley-Hamilton from Mathlib). minpoly_annihilates: aeval M (minpoly K M) = 0 (defining property). minpoly_divides_annihilator: universal property (minpoly.dvd). both_monic: both polynomials are monic.
sections.mathContext: $\text{Ann}(M) = (m_M)$ as a principal ideal in $K[X]$. $p(M) = 0 \Leftrightarrow m_M \mid p$.

sections.title: Parts 6–7: Root Relationship and Linear Map Connection
sections.summary: minpoly_root_is_charpoly_root: every root of minpoly is a root of charpoly. minpoly_eq_linmap_minpoly: minpoly of matrix = minpoly of corresponding linear map (Matrix.minpoly_toLin'). Establishes basis-independence of the minimal polynomial.
sections.mathContext: $\alpha$ root of $m_M \Rightarrow$ $\alpha$ root of $p_M$. $m_M = m_\phi$ where $\phi$ is the linear map represented by $M$.

sections.title: Parts 8–9: Concrete Examples and Uniqueness
sections.summary: identity_annihilated: aeval I (minpoly K I) = 0 (minpoly = X − 1). zero_annihilated: aeval 0 (minpoly K 0) = 0 (minpoly = X). zero_matrix_minpoly_dvd_charpoly: minpoly(0) | charpoly(0). minpoly_dvd_annihilating_monic: universal property restated. Identity and zero are the extremal cases with maximum degree gap n−1.
sections.mathContext: Identity: $m_I = X-1$, $p_I = (X-1)^n$. Zero: $m_0 = X$, $p_0 = X^n$. Both have degree gap $n-1$.

conclusion.summary: Minpoly-charpoly relationship fully formalized: 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Divisibility, annihilation, degree bounds, and root relationships all proved.
conclusion.implications: This provides the core infrastructure for Jordan normal form theory in Lean 4. The minpoly | charpoly relationship is fundamental to understanding diagonalizability (minpoly splits into distinct linear factors) vs. Jordan decomposition.
openQuestions: Can the Jordan normal form theorem be formalized in Lean 4 using this infrastructure?
Can the characterization of diagonalizable matrices (minpoly has no repeated roots) be proved?
Can the rational canonical form (based on minpoly factorization) be formalized?

crossReferences.description: Cayley-Hamilton (charpoly(M)(M) = 0) is the key ingredient: it makes charpoly an annihilating polynomial, from which minpoly | charpoly follows via the universal property
Companion entry formalizing minpoly reduction (any f(M) = f mod minpoly, evaluated at M) and the annihilator ideal Ann(M) = (minpoly) in K[X]
Cyclic vector theory: M has a cyclic vector iff minpoly(M) = charpoly(M), the case of minimum degree gap — complementary to the extremal examples (I, 0) where the gap is maximal
Polynomial reduction via minpoly: for any polynomial f, aeval M f = aeval M (f mod minpoly), leveraging the universal property proved here
